# A colon-refspec git push gets the guard's message in any shell form

## Context

From 17 to 19 Nov, every refused feature-branch push of one Claude seat came from a single command shape, `git -C <clone> push -u origin ada/X:ada/X`. On 19 Nov the auto-mode classifier refused that form as "Undermining Oversight" five times out of six. On the same branches, the plain `git push -u origin <branch>` passed five times out of five, two of those through `git -C`. The operator asked what blocks the pushes, then approved this fix.

The refusals and the passes are observed; they are that day's tool results. Why the classifier refuses the colon form is inferred. The project denies colon refspecs (`.claude/settings.template.json:46`, `Bash(git push* *:*)`), and `git -C <dir> push …` does not start with `git push`, so the glob never matches. The call then reaches the classifier as a refspec push that the settings forbid.

## The Problem

- **The deny glob only catches the literal prefix.** `git push … a:b` is denied with the permission layer's generic message. `git -C <dir> push … a:b` and `cd <dir> && git push … a:b` reach the classifier. Neither path tells the seat which form works.
- **A refused push stalls a lane.** The seat kept retrying the colon form across sessions. Its own notes prescribed it, reasoning that a new branch tracks `origin/dev`. That is true only of a bare `git push` with no branch named: `git push origin <branch>` pushes to the same-named remote branch.
- **Only Claude seats are affected.** `.codex/rules/pr-lifecycle.rules` prompts on `git push` and forbids only force pushes and dev/main destinations, and `.agents/ANTIGRAVITY_RULES.md` has no push rule.

## The Architectural Reality

- **The existing guard.** `.claude/hooks/gitCommitPushGuardHook.mjs` (#21290) is a `PreToolUse` Bash guard.
  - `gitSubcommands()` walks `scan(command).codes`, so quoted text, comments and heredoc bodies never count. It finds `git` in command position, skips its global options (`-C`, `-c`, `--git-dir` …), and returns only the subcommand names.
  - The guard is registered in `.claude/settings.template.json`, and its spec is `test/playwright/unit/hooks/gitCommitPushGuardHook.spec.mjs`.
- **The colon deny.** `.claude/settings.template.json:46` denies `Bash(git push* *:*)`. #14419 keeps colon refspecs denied as defense in depth beneath `npm run agent-push`. That wrapper accepts only `agent/*` branches, so seat branches such as `ada/*` push raw and stay classified.
- **The precedent.** #14419's Avoided Traps: "the parser is the boundary", not more globs.
- **Git's grammar.** `git push [<options>] [<repository> [<refspec>…]]`. The first positional is the remote, and a URL remote may contain a `:`. Only later positionals are refspecs.
- **Design authority.** `.claude/settings.template.json:46` (colon refspecs are denied) and #14419. This ticket makes that rule hold in every shell form and names the form that works.

## The Fix

In `gitCommitPushGuardHook.mjs`, the parser returns each git invocation's subcommand together with its arguments. A `push` whose refspec positional (after the remote) contains a `:` is blocked with a message that does two things:
- It names the denied rule.
- It gives the working forms: `git push -u origin <branch>`, which reaches the same-named remote branch even when the local branch tracks `origin/dev`; for a commit with no branch, `git branch <name> <sha>` first.

The module's summary covers both checks. There is no new hook file and no settings change, because the hook is already registered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] These are blocked with the message (unit):
  - `git -C <dir> push -u origin a/b:a/b`
  - `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/x`
  - `cd <dir> && git push origin x:x`
  - a push of `"<sha>:refs/heads/x"`
- [ ] These pass (unit):
  - `git push -u origin ada/x`
  - `git -C <dir> push origin ada/x`
  - a push to a URL remote (`git push https://github.com/o/r.git x`)
  - a push option holding a colon (`--push-option=ci:skip`)
  - quoted text or a commit message naming `a:b`
- [ ] The commit-and-push check behaves as before, and its existing cases pass unchanged.
- [ ] Receipts at the PR head: `npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.mjs test/playwright/unit/hooks`.

## Out of Scope

- Classifier policy and allow rules (#20796).
- The deny glob itself, `npm run agent-push`, and the Codex and Antigravity rules.
- Force pushes and `+` refspecs.

## Avoided Traps

- **More deny globs** (`Bash(git -C * push* *:*)` …). That is #14419's whack-a-mole trap, and a glob still answers with the generic denial.
- **An allow rule for seat-branch pushes.** It widens what skips the classifier. That is the operator's call, not this fix.

## Related

#21290 (the guard) · #14419 (the refspec wrapper; the colon deny as defense in depth) · #20796 (the `autoMode` block is never read)
